mode_evidence: The first practice is explicitly mind's-eye work: eyes closed, attention on the heart, 'with the eyes of the heart see the picture of the Master'. The translator glosses these as 'thought-forms'. The form seen after closing the eyes is then treated as the soul of the form and a key to Malakut, which hints at crossing into perceived forms, but the text never says the image becomes seen in the visual field. The only light report ('subtle illumination in thy heart, and in all thy body') is a bodily sensation, not clearly a seen light.
onset_evidence: For a seeker with nothing: find a solitary corner, form a picture of a revered faqir or loved one, close the eyes, fix attention on the heart. Long persistence is said to make the picture 'definite and clear' and then to show pictures never seen before. Alongside this comes breath retention with La ilaha / Illa 'llah. No time scale except the teacher's years of breath-holding. Grace is mentioned in general terms; transmission through a chain is stressed for the breath practice.

conditions.posture: Sit with elbows on knees; thumbs close the ears, index fingers hold the eyelids shut without pressing the eyeballs, ring and little fingers seal the lips, middle fingers work the nostrils.
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Eyes closed; attention on the heart (cedar heart, left chest), or on the colourless spherical heart in the brain if distractions trouble.
conditions.setting: Retired, solitary spot; cave or desert for the sound practice.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Hold the breath as long as comfortable and lengthen slowly; the teacher held one breath from evening to morning prayer for fifteen years.
conditions.prerequisites: A master or lineage; the practice is said to come by authentic descent.
conditions.other: Recite La ilah on inhaling and Il allah on exhaling.

stages.label: Alam-i-misal
stages.description: Thought-picture of the master seen with the heart's eyes; when clear, it opens onto Malakut.

stages.label: Alam-i-malakut
stages.description: Forms of prophets, saints, angels appear in the polished heart-mirror; do not rest or seek miracles there.

stages.label: breath-retention effects
stages.description: Heat, buoyancy, delight and a subtle illumination in heart and whole body.

what_to_do_with_light: Observe the Malakut appearances minutely, but do not stay entangled or desire clairvoyance and miracles; the aim lies beyond.
obstacles_and_fixes: Distracting 'dangers' in the cedar heart: move attention to the colourless spherical heart in the brain.
Higher fix: treat the distracting form as one's own self so it ceases to be a danger.
Breath expelled too fast harms the lungs; expel slowly.
cautions: Do not be absorbed in the Malakut world or seek phenomena and miracles.
Breath retention is not to be pushed to suffocation.
interpretation: The images are thought-forms of the plane of counterparts, a gateway to the subtle world whose forms are souls; the heart is a mirror that brightens as rust is removed.
practice_summary: Sit alone in a quiet corner and picture a revered teacher or a loved person. Close the eyes, fix attention on the heart and see the form with the eyes of the heart. Keep at it long and steadily until the picture is definite and clear, and expect further, unfamiliar forms to follow. For a stronger practice, with a teacher's authorisation, sit with elbows on the knees and seal ears, eyelids (without pressing the eyeballs), lips and nostrils with the fingers. Inhale through the left nostril reciting La ilah, draw the breath from the brain down to the heart, close both nostrils and hold as long as comfortable, then release slowly through the right nostril reciting Il allah, and alternate sides. After some time heat, buoyancy, delight and a subtle illumination in heart and body are said to arise, with inner sounds. If distraction troubles, shift attention to the brain centre.

key_passages.anchor: He must close his eyes and fix his attention on his heart, and with the eyes of the heart
key_passages.paraphrase: Close the eyes, fix attention on the heart, and see the master's or beloved's picture with the heart's eyes.
key_passages.quote: He must close his eyes and fix his attention on his heart, and with the eyes of the heart see the picture of the Master or the beloved.

key_passages.anchor: The picture of the form, which is seen after closing the eyes, is understood to be the soul of that form
key_passages.paraphrase: The form seen after closing the eyes is treated as the soul of the form, not a body, and the thought-picture plane is the key to Malakut.

key_passages.anchor: With the two index fingers shut the two eyes, in such a way, that the upper eyelid may remain steadily fixed on the lower eyelid
key_passages.paraphrase: Eyes are held shut by the index fingers resting on the lids, explicitly without pressing the eyeballs, during breath retention.

key_passages.paraphrase: After some practice of breath retention, heat, buoyancy, delight and a subtle illumination in heart and body are felt.
